- opened 2026-08-02 | **`merge=union` on this ledger makes GitHub call EVERY ledger-touching PR conflicted, while every git client merges it cleanly — and the documented escape fails too** | `.gitattributes` on main declares `.claude/skills/modus/PENDING-ARMS.md merge=union`, a BUILT-IN git driver that resolves by keeping both sides' lines — exactly right for an append-only registry, and the reason no session has ever hand-resolved this file. But GitHub's mergeability computation does **not** apply `.gitattributes` merge drivers: it runs a plain three-way merge and reports `mergeable: false` / `mergeStateStatus: DIRTY`. Measured on PR #3527 with both sides looking at the SAME base (`04b3eb38e`) and the SAME head (`aa7d97029`): GitHub said `dirty`, `git merge --no-commit` succeeded cleanly in BOTH directions, and `gh pr update-branch` — the documented server-side fix — failed with "Cannot update PR branch due to conflicts". The only path is a LOCAL merge of main into the branch, then a push (on M5 that costs a full pre-push suite). The danger is not the delay: a session reading `mergeable: false` as a real conflict will either burn a cycle hunting a conflict that does not exist, or — far worse — hand-edit the ledger to "resolve" it and drop the other side's lines, which is precisely the loss `merge=union` was added to prevent. Verified on this merge that the driver does its job: 269 open rows on the branch + 265 on main -> **270** after, nothing lost, `phantom_operator=0 malformed=0`. TECH-DEBT (low severity, high confusion cost, recurs on every PR that touches the ledger — i.e. most of them) | **RUNBOOK HALF ARMED 2026-08-04 (healer tick, Mini)**: `docs/runbooks/merge-queue-discipline.md` §6quinquies now states the fact verbatim (DIRTY is expected on a ledger-touching PR, `gh pr update-branch` fails, local `git merge origin/main` + push is the only path) — proof: `grep -n "6quinquies" docs/runbooks/merge-queue-discipline.md` on `origin/main` after this PR merges. **CHECK BUILT 2026-08-08 (infra-lane session, PR #3838; checkout+watcher fix same day, follow-up PR)**: `scripts/check_ledger_no_silent_loss.py` + `.github/workflows/check-ledger-no-silent-loss.yml` — flags an open row present at merge-base AND on current origin/main (untouched by ANY PR since the branch diverged) that's missing from HEAD; skips entirely on a PR that doesn't touch the ledger. Deliberately narrower than "every main row must survive" (this ledger's own header sanctions legitimate removal on proof-of-armed, and no git-history check can tell that apart from an accidental drop) — non-required/dry-run by design (`continue-on-error: true`), same promotion path as `check-kbli-dataset-sync.yml`. Guilt+innocence self-tested every run (`scripts/tests/test_check_ledger_no_silent_loss.py`, 4 cases incl. a scripted reproduction of the exact incident class). PR #3838's own first CI run caught two self-inflicted defects live (both non-required, neither blocked the merge queue): (1) the workflow checked out `base.sha` instead of `head.sha`, so the script + test files this very PR introduces were physically absent from the checkout — "file or directory not found", exit 4, on PR #3838 itself; (2) the new workflow wasn't registered in `main-push-failure-watch.yml`'s `workflows:` list, failing `check_watcher_coverage.py`'s self-conformance gate. Both fixed same-day in the immediate follow-up PR. missing arming step (residual, NOT closed): (1) observe the dry-run signal over real ledger-touching PRs for false positives before promoting; (2) promotion to a required branch-protection check is operator-only (repo/branch-protection settings, CLAUDE.md §13) — not something a session can arm itself | me (sessione M5) for the original finding; me (healer, Mini) for the runbook half; me (sessione M5, infra-lane) for the check + its same-day fix; operator[gui] for eventual promotion to required (branch-protection settings, GitHub UI) | proof-of-armed: a session hitting DIRTY on a ledger PR reaches the local-merge instruction without re-deriving it (ARMED, see grep above); "a merge that loses open rows is caught" (CHECK ARMED — dry-run, self-test genuinely runs against the PR's own new files as of the follow-up fix; PROMOTION TO REQUIRED not armed, needs observation window + operator action)

- opened 2026-08-01 | **CodeQL findings cannot block a merge in this repo, and the obvious way to make them block BREAKS THE MERGE QUEUE — measured, by breaking it** | The two required contexts `CodeQL Analysis (python|javascript)` are matrix JOB completions: they go green whatever the scan found, so they prove the scanner RAN, never that it found nothing. Earlier this session I promoted the aggregate `CodeQL` context to required (26 -> 27) to close that. **It hung the entire merge queue.** #3496 sat at position 1 in `AWAITING_CHECKS` for ~50 minutes with 38/38 checks green on the queue ref and exactly one required context missing — `CodeQL` — with a sibling lane's #3460 stacked behind it, and every PR opened afterwards would have hit the same wall. Cause, verified rather than guessed: that check is posted by the GitHub **code-scanning app** (`app.id 57789`) when it processes the SARIF **for a pull request**; a merge-queue ref is not a PR, so it is never posted there — the requirement is unsatisfiable by construction, not flaky. `security.yml` already declares `merge_group:` and its matrix jobs DO report on the queue ref, which is exactly what made the gap invisible. Reverted to 26 contexts and confirmed server-side; the queue drained to 0 within minutes. **The lesson is mine and is the one I keep writing**: I ran a positive control before arming it — "does code scanning attribute alerts to a pull ref?" — and answered it only on the PR path, never on the merge_group path. A gate must be proven on EVERY ref that has to satisfy it. Also dead for the same reason: a PR-scoped gate that queries the alerts API, built and abandoned earlier today when its own positive control showed no alert is ever attributed to a pull ref. TECH-DEBT | missing arming step: a mechanism that survives the merge queue — the only shapes that can work are (a) a job in OUR workflow (so it runs on `merge_group`) that fails on new high/critical by diffing the alert set against the base, if and only if the alerts API can be made to answer for a merge ref, or (b) accept that blocking is impossible and arm DETECTION instead: a post-merge job on `main` that alarms on any new high/critical, which is honest about being after-the-fact. Do NOT re-promote the `CodeQL` context under any circumstances | me (sessione M5, follow-up lane) | proof-of-armed: for (a), a PR carrying a deliberately introduced high-severity finding goes red AND a clean PR still merges through the queue; for (b), an alarm delivered to the Telegram gateway for a real new alert on main, plus a green run proving the detector is not vacuous

- opened 2026-08-01 | **The S03 API-key hardening is entirely vestigial in production — dead for TWO independent reasons, and a CodeQL verdict was reached on a false claim that it is live** | Found while triaging the two `py/weak-sensitive-data-hashing` alerts on `api_key_auth.py` (#4669, #4670). The lane's own reason asserts the code is "executed on every incoming request carrying an API key that isn't in the in-memory legacy map, i.e. it's on the live authentication path". **Measured: it is not.** (a) `validate_api_key_enhanced` guards BOTH its DB branches with `if conn:`, and no production caller ever passes one — `backend/app/auth/validation.py:147` calls `validate_api_key(x_api_key)` with a single argument and the parameter defaults to `None`; grepped every non-test call site of both names, there is no other. (b) Even with a connection, the table is absent: `to_regclass('public.api_key_records')` is NULL, 0 rows in `information_schema.tables` (positive control: the same role sees `clients` and `documents`), and migration **089 was never applied** — absent from `_schema_versions`, which has 186 rows spanning 0-261 with a gap where 89 should be (85..95 contains only 92). Empirical confirmation: 0 occurrences of either `S03:` log line in the live `nuzantara-rag` stream, against a positive control of 100 lines carried. So the believed-shipped hardening (DB-backed roles, auto-migration of legacy keys, per-key revocation via `is_active`) does nothing, and the system runs entirely on the legacy in-memory name-based map. Superscar #2 on an AUTH surface. **The two CodeQL alerts are deliberately NOT dismissed**: the hash is unreachable today, but "unreachable" is a property of the wiring, not of the code — wiring a `conn` later would make them live silently. Note also the shape question they raise is not "use bcrypt": an API key lookup must be deterministic (`WHERE key_hash = $1`), so a per-key salt is impossible by construction; if the keys stay low-entropy human-chosen (repo convention, cf. the rotated `zantara-secret-2024`), the right primitive is HMAC-SHA256 with a server-side pepper in Fly secrets, which keeps O(1) lookup and defeats offline rainbow-tabling. TECH-DEBT | missing arming step: a DECISION first, because both directions are legitimate and the wrong one is worse than the status quo — either (a) arm S03 properly (apply 089, thread a connection from the auth dependency, decide the hash primitive, plan the legacy cutover) or (b) delete the dead path and its tests so nothing claims a protection that does not exist. - opened 2026-07-16 | pre-push DB clone did not inherit the template's owner — the gate armed last night (#2489) was blocking EVERY push on M5 (fix committed, PR pending). `CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE` re-parents the clone to the creating role (the OS user, `balizero`), and since PG15 `public` is owned by pg_database_owner → resolves to the DB owner → a template owned by `test` loses test's CREATE on public inside the clone. Table ownership is copied; a privilege held implicitly THROUGH ownership is not (an explicit GRANT would have been). 39 failed + 79 errors of 17339, all "permission denied for schema public" + its "relation does not exist" cascade. Latent from #2489 until nuzantara_test was re-created with owner=test at 11:38 today — between two of my own pushes that passed, which is why it looked like my markdown-only commit had broken pytest. Class #2/#3: a fresh guard failing closed on innocent work; and #9, since ownership is a PROXY for the privilege, not the privilege. The local template got an explicit `GRANT USAGE, CREATE ON SCHEMA public TO test` (survives cloning, unlike ownership) as the immediate unblock — that is LOCAL M5 state, so Pro/Mini or any re-bootstrap still needs the hook fix. NOT yet armed fleet-wide: git resolves hooksPath against the MAIN checkout, so this bites only once merged AND pulled on each machine. | me (sessione M5) | proof-of-armed: on a clean template owned by `test` with no explicit grant, the OLD clone path gives owner=balizero / test CREATE=false / `ERROR: permission denied for schema public` and the NEW path gives owner=test / CREATE=true / `CREATE TABLE` — plus the three suites that failed the blocked push (crm/partners, compliance alerts_engine, war_room migration_112) at 69 passed against a clone; fleet-armed when `git log -1 .husky/pre-push` on Pro and Mini shows this commit

- closed 2026-07-24 | NEW SCAR (candidate W103, family #9 State-schema mutation drift — a proxy lied about state) — PR #2961 spent ~6 rounds (~1.5h wall-clock) of merge-origin/main→regen-docs→prettier→push, with `gh pr view 2961` persistently reporting `mergeStateStatus: DIRTY`/`mergeable: CONFLICTING` after every single push, despite the diff visibly resolving each time. Root cause: the local/worktree branch had silently drifted in NAME from the PR's actual tracked branch — pushes were landing on `agent/air-m5/mouth/gate-deadlines-repair`, a branch with no PR at all, while PR #2961 tracks `agent/air-m5/mouth/gate-deadlines` (no `-repair` suffix), whose head (`5d8eeadc2d`) never moved. `gh pr view --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus` compares whatever `head.ref` the PR object holds against ever-moving `main` and reports its cached-feeling verdict without ever surfacing the ref name itself in the default view — so the tool kept answering truthfully about the WRONG branch, and nothing in the normal `gh pr view` output flags a branch-name mismatch; it reads exactly like "your merge attempt failed again." Diagnostic breakthrough: dropping to the raw REST object — `gh api repos/Balizero1987/Teman2/pulls/2961 --jq '{head_sha:.head.sha, ref:.head.ref, mergeable, mergeable_state}'` — immediately exposed `ref: "agent/air-m5/mouth/gate-deadlines"`, i.e. NOT the branch being pushed to. Fixed: confirmed the real PR branch was a strict ancestor of the repair-branch HEAD (`git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/agent/air-m5/mouth/gate-deadlines HEAD`, safe fast-forward, 0 data loss across 368 files/+22307-3845), force-pushed the correct target (`git push origin HEAD:agent/air-m5/mouth/gate-deadlines`), renamed the local branch to match, and set upstream tracking so the drift can't silently recur for the rest of the session. General antidote for the family: **when a PR shows persistently-DIRTY/CONFLICTING status that content-diffing says should be clean, don't re-run the standard fix loop a 3rd time — go straight to `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<N>` and diff `head.ref` against `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`/`git remote get-url` push target before touching anything else.** Candidate for promotion into `.claude/rules/cicatrix-superscar.md` family #9 (or its own #11 if it recurs) — not added to that file this session (out of scope: PENDING-ARMS is the fast capture, superscar promotion is a deliberate curation step) | missing arming step: (1) operator/session review + promote into cicatrix-superscar.md family #9 MEMBRI if judged non-orphan; (2) consider a cheap guard — `git remote get-url origin` + local-branch-name vs any open PR's `head.ref` for that branch — surfaced by `stop_verify.py` or a pre-push hint when they diverge | owner: me (follow-up session, CAPTURE→promotion step) | proof-of-armed: `cicatrix-superscar.md` family #9 (or new #11) MEMBRI line references this discovery, or `scar query "branch mismatch"` returns a hit

- closed 2026-07-26 | the PENDING-ARMS ledger itself carried an unresolved diff3 conflict marker on main (`||||||| parent of d47b541b78`, line 490) — and it was NOT cosmetic: the marker's seven pipes are parsed as fields, so `pending_arms_report.py` read the entry above it with `owner=?` and swallowed the entry below it (the INTERACTIVE-DEFAULT ruling) outright, while the report's own `## MALFORMED` section still said `none`. A SECOND, independent stray marker (`||||||| ebfbd71019`, the ledger's own last line, no matching `<<<<<<<`/`=======`/`>>>>>>>` anywhere) was found the same day: it blanked the owner of the 'Bali disclosure is hover-only' entry directly above it (measured live before this fix: `owner=''`, `proof='ebfbd71019'`, `cls=TECH-DEBT`, `bucket=FRESH` — invisible to both `--strict` and `--strict-phantom`, proving the residue below was real and not yet closed by the first marker's removal). Both markers are now gone. Structural fix landed in `pending_arms_report.py`: (1) `parse_entry` flags an empty (genuinely blank) owner as MALFORMED rather than silently degrading to `owner=?`; (2) `extract_open_entries` refuses to absorb a conflict-marker-shaped line (`CONFLICT_MARKER_RE`, 3 shapes — `<<<<<<<`/`|||||||`/`>>>>>>>`) into the entry being built — finalizes the entry in progress first (protecting it from corruption) and surfaces the marker as its own MALFORMED entry instead of silently dropping it; (3) both `--strict` and `--strict-phantom` now exit 1 on >=1 MALFORMED entry, not just >=1 PHANTOM-OPERATOR. Cross-family review (Codex gpt-5.6-terra, same day) caught two more real gaps in the first pass and BOTH were handled properly rather than rubber-stamped: (P1) a 4-field entry omitting the owner segment entirely back-anchors the missing_step text into owner undetected — the obvious fix (raise the pipe-count floor from `< 3` to the canonical `< 5`) was DRAFTED, then REJECTED after measuring it against the real ledger: 45/225 open entries (20%) use a different, legitimate 4-field shape (artifact + owner + proof, no missing_step — mostly FIREBREAK-style) with correctly-extracted real owners, and the floor would have flagged all 45 as MALFORMED — a far worse regression than the gap it closed. Left open, deliberately, pinned by `test_known_gap_four_field_entry_missing_owner_segment_not_caught`. (P2, FIXED) `CONFLICT_MARKER_RE`'s line-anchor alone could not tell a real orphaned marker from one deliberately quoted inside a ` ``` ` fenced code block to illustrate it — `extract_open_entries` tracks fence state and exempts marker-shaped lines while fenced (still absorbed as literal content); also dropped bare `=======` from the detected shapes (valid Markdown Setext-divider syntax too, and never the shape either live marker actually took). A third bug surfaced by the review's own test corpus: `>>>>>>>` also starts with `>` and was being silently swallowed by the pre-existing blockquote branch before ever reaching the marker check — fixed by reordering the branches. SECOND review pass (same day) on the corrected diff caught a fourth, more severe bug in the fence guard's first draft: it exempted ALL structural checks while fenced (not just the marker check), so a fence that never closes would silently absorb every subsequent line — including every later real entry — until EOF, with zero MALFORMED signal (`--strict-phantom` stays green while the rest of the ledger vanishes from the parse). Narrowed to exempt ONLY the marker check while fenced: entry-start/list-item/blank/heading detection now stay active regardless of fence state, so an unclosed fence degrades safely (worst case: a genuine marker after the accidental open goes uncaught until EOF, same class of accepted trade-off as the dropped `=======` shape) instead of catastrophically. Residual documented-not-fixed gaps in the fence guard, none reproducible in the real corpus today (zero fences of any kind currently exist in this ledger): `~~~`-style fences unrecognized, a fence closes on ANY >=3-backtick run regardless of the opening run's exact length, and 4-space-indented code blocks (no backticks) are invisible to it since `strip()` removes the indentation first | owner: me (immune-forge lane, follow-up) | proof-of-armed: `pytest scripts/tests/test_pending_arms_report.py` green (68 tests, incl. `test_innocence_unclosed_fence_does_not_swallow_the_rest_of_the_ledger` and `test_real_ledger_has_zero_malformed_after_conflict_marker_cure`) — the real ledger carries zero MALFORMED entries and `--strict-phantom` exits 0; `--strict` still correctly exits 1 on pre-existing unrelated overdue tech-debt, unchanged

- closed 2026-07-27 | **RETRACTED THE SAME NIGHT — "the prod-Postgres primary is ~10x degraded" was my wrong diagnosis; it was shared-cpu BURST-CREDIT exhaustion, largely self-inflicted.** What I measured was real: the primary took 16-31s to gzip 128MB where the replica took 5s, its Fly `vm` check was failing with `cpu: system spent 3.13s of the last 10 seconds waiting on cpu`, `/proc/pressure/cpu` read `some avg60 ~35-46` with io-pressure ~0, and the nightly dump of an unchanged 2749MB database went from ~90s to ~1150s. What I CONCLUDED from it — a contended host needing a restart or replacement — was wrong, and a cross-family review seat (Codex GPT-5.6, xhigh) refused the premise: on `shared-cpu-2x` a machine gets ~10ms per 80ms once burst credit is spent (~1/8 of a continuous CPU). **An idle replica has full credit; a primary that has just run hours of `pg_dump | gzip` has none.** My "controlled comparison" held command, region, machine size and minute constant and missed the one variable that mattered. DECISIVE TEST: after ~70 minutes idle the primary did the identical work in **5s, the same as the replica**, with CPU pressure down to `some avg60=1.33` and guest-visible steal advancing 4 ticks. A contended host does not heal by idling; a replenishing budget does. The clue was already in my own numbers, read as noise: 25.8s -> 30.8s -> 16s -> 5s, tracking idle time. (Panel note: a second seat, Gemini 3.1 Pro, called PSI "definitive proof" of hypervisor contention — over-reading it, since `pressure/cpu some` counts tasks waiting for CPU whatever the cause. The seat that questioned my premise was the right one. Kimi was out of quota: a dead seat, not a dissenting one.) | missing arming step: **none — there is no fault to arm against here.** The ~1150s dump is expected behaviour for sustained compression on a shared-cpu machine, and the raised timeouts already absorb it. If the dump duration is ever judged unacceptable the levers are (a) dump from the REPLICA so the primary keeps its credit, or (b) a `performance-*` CPU for whichever node dumps — both are cost/design calls, not incident response. What DOES remain open is the separate quorum finding in the entry below | owner: me (closed by measurement, kept for the lesson) | proof-of-armed: n/a — retracted. The standing lesson: "identical machines, same minute" is not a controlled comparison when the resource under test is a budget that refills; ask what state each side accumulated BEFORE the measurement, and treat a metric that only says "waiting" as a symptom, never a cause | ledger-hygiene 2026-08-07: prefix flipped `opened`→`closed` (content otherwise untouched) — this line was written as a self-retraction but kept the `- opened` prefix, so `scripts/pending_arms_report.py` counted it as open TECH-DEBT for 11 days (meta-ledger-closed-as-new-opened-lines, family #9 W88-adjacent). - opened 2026-08-03 | **`branch_graveyard_cleanup.sh` categorises 0 of 39 merged branches — its four buckets cannot see the dominant case** | Ran the report on 2026-08-03 with 45 local branches, 39 of which have a MERGED PR: output was `0 / 0 / 0 / 0`. Not a lie and not a broken probe — honest for its own definitions, which is the problem. "Merged & deletable (SHA ancestor of main)" cannot fire because the repo squash-merges, so a branch tip is never an ancestor. "Content-on-main & deletable (diff vs main empty or pure-deletion)" cannot fire either, because after the squash lands main keeps advancing and the same files gain later changes, so the diff is non-empty for reasons that have nothing to do with the branch. The two age buckets (>30d `claude/*`, >90d others) miss anything recent. So the ordinary, healthy branch — squash-merged last week — falls through all four and the tool reports a clean graveyard over a 39-branch backlog. The decisive probe that DOES work was found the same day and is cheap: compare local `HEAD` against `gh pr view <n> --json headRefOid` — equal means everything local was merged, and `git log <merged>..HEAD` counts anything beyond it. TECH-DEBT | missing arming step: add a fifth category keyed on the merged PR's `headRefOid` rather than on tree comparison, so recent squash-merges are classified instead of silently skipped; keep it REPORT-ONLY like the zombie buckets until it has run clean for a cycle | me (healer, Mini, 2026-08-04 — CODE ARMED, LIVE PROOF STILL PARTIAL) | proof-of-armed: category 5 (`pr_merged_match()`, one `gh pr list --state merged` call, matched by ref name + oid PREFIX so abbreviated for-each-ref shas line up with full gh oids) implemented + guilt/innocence unit-tested (`scripts/tests/test_branch_graveyard_prmerged.sh`, 6/6 pass: real ref+oid-prefix matches; same ref with a stale/wrong oid does not; a real oid under the wrong ref does not; absent gh-pr-list fixture degrades to no-match, not a crash; tripwires the live matcher + report-only wiring). - opened 2026-08-10 | **The consent that SYMBIOSIS Law 2 now leans on is DECIDED, not implemented — and the first draft said "gap CHIUSO"** | Zero ruled on 2026-08-09 that explicit client consent is collected always, by contract, as a condition of service, so cross-border PII transit stops being a gate on vendor choice. That business decision is real and binding. What is NOT real yet is the control: there is **no contractual clause drafted, no per-client evidence service, no withdrawal mechanism, and no pre-provider enforcement** — and the status of the Google Workspace DPA (the safeguard rung of the Art. 56 cascade, which `CLAUDE.md` §14 pairs with consent as an internal rule) has never been verified or recorded anywhere in this repo. `apps/backend-rag/backend/migrations/migration_091_client_consent_log.py` only declares a legacy table; no runtime service or caller consumes it, so its presence is not evidence that consent or withdrawal is armed. `cloud_vision_gate` is also not that control: it governs only cloud OCR/vision fallbacks for documents and images. Chat-text inference is processing plus transfer when the text contains PII, and the current gateway has no shared ingress check that joins data provenance to a demonstrable per-transfer Art. 56 basis. A blind reuse of the response-side PII scanner at one router would neither establish that basis nor cover direct gateway callers. The safe rule is therefore fail-closed — keep client PII local/off-cloud or abstain while the basis is not demonstrable — but the repository does not yet enforce that rule for chat, so the gap remains explicit rather than being mislabeled an accepted risk or a compliant state. The rewrite keeps Zero's decision verbatim, preserves the statutory adequacy → binding safeguard → consent hierarchy, and separates the stricter no-cleartext-output policy (Artt. 35-39 duties) from the distinct Art. 56 transfer question. This entry exists so the distance between "policy decided" and "control armed" stays visible: a legal control is subject to superscar #2 exactly like a cron | missing arming step: (1) draft + adopt the consent clause in the service contract — `operator[business]`, Zero's call, no session can write a term of trade; (2) verify and RECORD the Workspace DPA/SCC status (which agreement, accepted when, by which account) — `operator[business]`, it needs the Workspace admin console; (3) build and verify the per-client basis/evidence service plus withdrawal path, reusing the legacy schema only after confirming its live status and suitability; (4) place a context-aware fail-closed check at the true shared pre-provider boundary, with explicit provenance and an off-cloud/abstain fallback rather than a router-local regex patch | owner: operator[business] for (1) and (2), session for (3) and (4) after the required evidence exists | proof-of-armed: tests show client PII is blocked before every provider call when no Art. 56 basis is demonstrable, allowed only with a valid evidence record, and blocked again after withdrawal; the DPA status is written down in this repo instead of being assumed — until then `SYMBIOSIS.md` Law 2 and `CLAUDE.md` §14 say "condotta richiesta, non stato implementato" and that wording must not be softened

- open 2026-08-10 | **A test conftest hijacks `sys.modules["backend.app.core.config"]`, so the same test is green or red depending on WHICH tests you asked for** | `backend/tests/unit/services/rag/agentic/conftest.py` installs a fake `backend.app.core.config` module whose `settings` is a bare `MagicMock`, guarded only by `if "backend.app.core.config" not in sys.modules`. Conftests are imported during collection, before any test module, so in a PARTIAL run that names that directory the hijack wins the race and every later import of the real config gets the mock. The mock sets ~30 attributes but not `COMPANY_NAME`, so any code doing `settings.COMPANY_NAME.lower()` raises `TypeError: 'in <string>' requires string as left operand, not MagicMock`. Measured today: `pytest backend/tests/services/rag/agentic/ <two unit files>` → **43 failed**; the same tests under full-tree collection (`pytest backend/tests/ -k …`, the CI shape) → **64 passed, 0 failed**, because by then the real config is already in `sys.modules` and the guard takes its no-op branch. So CI is honest and the local partial run is the liar — which is the dangerous direction: it cost this session ~20 minutes and nearly got read as a defect in the diff under test (W107, the probe that measures a disease can have it). NOT cured here on purpose: adding `COMPANY_NAME` to the mock would turn today's loud symptom into a quieter one and leave the next unset attribute to bite the same way — the defect is the hijack, not the missing key. The proportionate cure is to delete the `sys.modules` surgery and let the directory use the same real-config fixture the rest of the suite uses, which is a test-infrastructure change with its own blast radius and does not belong bundled with a client-facing fix | missing arming step: replace the `sys.modules` hijack in that conftest with the suite's normal config fixture, then prove partial and full runs agree | owner: me (sessione M5) | proof-of-armed: the 43-vs-0 divergence above collapses — the same selection reports the same result whether invoked as a partial run or under full-tree collection
